heroHeadline: ARTEMIS III CREW REVEAL 7 DAYS AWAY (JUNE 9, JSC) — LC-36 SATELLITE IMAGERY: TRANSPORTER-ERECTOR DESTROYED, NO REBUILD TIMELINE; IFT-12 INVESTIGATION ONGOING; CREW DAY 53
heroSubtitle: June 2: Planet Labs SkySat satellite imagery published June 1–2 reveals the full extent of damage at Blue Origin's LC-36, Cape Canaveral — four days after New Glenn's catastrophic explosion during a prelaunch static fire test on May 29. The transporter-erector is destroyed, one lightning tower collapsed, and the main launch tower shows bent structural members. Industry analysts and local reporters reached no consensus on a rebuild timeline, with estimates ranging from months to over a year; Blue Origin has issued no formal restoration schedule. Since New Glenn is the sole vehicle for the Blue Moon Mark 1 Endurance cargo lander (NASA Moon Base I contract, $188M), Moon Base I's fall 2026 delivery to Shackleton Connecting Ridge remains on hold. The Artemis III crew announcement is 7 days away (June 9, 11 a.m. EDT, JSC, NASA+/YouTube) — the four astronauts selected for the redesignated Earth-orbit rendezvous-and-docking test mission (targeting late 2027) will be publicly named for the first time. The FAA's mishap investigation into Starship IFT-12's Booster 19 boostback burn failure (May 22) remains open; IFT-13 is blocked from a flight license until SpaceX's corrective-action report is approved, with return-to-flight projected no earlier than July–August 2026. This continues to delay the orbital propellant transfer demonstration (mandatory Artemis III HLS qualification milestone) to Q3-Q4 2026. The Artemis II crew — Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch, Canadian Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen — are on Day 53 post-splashdown at JSC, continuing reconditioning. The Artemis II Orion is in de-servicing at KSC's Multi-Payload Processing Facility; heat shield shipment to Marshall Space Flight Center is scheduled for this summer. House Appropriations markup (May 13) recommends $24.438B for NASA flat with FY2026 — rejecting the White House's 23% cut. Artemis Accords: 67 signatories (Paraguay 67th, May 7). CLPS 2.0 RFP responses due June 30.
